If falling from a great height, would wearing a full suit of knight armor be helpful or detrimental?

Up to what speed?

Terminal velocity depends on cross section (which would hardly change from a suit of armor) and mass (which would greatly be increased by a suit of armor).

Your terminal velocity with armor is higher and possibly more deadly, unless the suit compensates for the extra energy upon impact....
You would accelerate at the same rate. It would probably contain some of the splash when you hit though.

At best it would restrict movement, so the limbs wouldn't flail. Potentially causing more damage if the body landed on the arm. I cannot see it being helpful or detrimental. I'm assuming great height equates to a height that will allow one to achieve terminal velocity. With that in mind, one will still have the same impact where on would land. Now I assume the armor will have some padding on the inside (that way it can take multiple strikes and still protect the wearer) so that might have some help reducing the impact. However since it isn't designed for this type of impact I doubt it would do much.

TL:DR Cannot see it helping since

  • It's not designed for that type of impact
  • You will still hit terminal velocity, regardless of the extra weight
  • At best it would restrict movement and reduce limbs landing under body.

Terminal velocity will be different with the suit of armor because of the added weight, unless the aerodynamics are bad enough to counter it. Terminal velocity is simply the point where the wind resistance matches gravity, so the object falls at a constant speed instead of accelerating.
